Here's the FigDown source for the BGP session reset procedure flowchart. I followed the router's instruction to treat `flowchart` decisions/branches as first-class constructs (process / decision / terminator node kinds, with edges carrying the yes/no branch labels), per the standard flowchart vocabulary this file's genre implies.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "BGP session reset procedure"

process checkcounters "Check interface error counters"
decision errorsfound "Errors found?"
process clearcounters "Clear interface counters"
terminator monitor "Monitor session"
terminator escalate "Escalate to human operator"

checkcounters -> errorsfound
errorsfound -> clearcounters "yes"
errorsfound -> escalate "no"
clearcounters -> monitor
```

Notes:
- `flowchart` is EXPERIMENTAL (experimental) per the router table, dispatchable at `figdown 0.1` — this is a deliberate, stated choice of genre for a decision procedure with two terminal outcomes, not a portability default.
- Node ids match exactly what was specified: `checkcounters`, `errorsfound`, `clearcounters`, `monitor`, `escalate`.
- The two branches out of `errorsfound` are labeled `"yes"`/`"no"` on the edges themselves, per the described yes/no branching.
- Labels are kept short (the operator-facing detail — "session keeps flapping," troubleshooting rationale — belongs in surrounding prose, not crammed into the figure).

Before committing, run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js bgp-session-reset.fd` to validate against the actual `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` keyword set (node-kind names and edge-label syntax may differ slightly from what's shown here if my assumptions about that file's exact spellings are off) — fix any `Line N:` errors it reports, then embed the resulting SVG with the standard `source:` footer.
